It fired `getProducts()` and `getStock()` separately. The stock handler only merged into the list if the products had already loaded (`list && list.map(...)`). When stock came back first, the merge was dropped, and the row then fell back to `stock ?? 0`, which reads as \"Out of stock\". I changed it to `Promise.all([getProducts(), getStock()])` and set the items once, with stock merged in. I also removed the `?? 0` fallback, so a missing stock value shows no label instead of a false \"Out of stock\". In the running app the list now shows a mix, matching `/stock`: Desk lamp, Ladder and Mug are \"In stock\", while Lantern (p2) and Notebook (p7), both at 0, are \"Out of stock\".
